text:
Ava (Head of Product): follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/packaging 1 drop quick Qs here about credits, rate limits, and burst policies and we'll capture answers for the public FAQ.

Nina (Customer Success): customer asked if promo/dev credits can be applied to Dedicated usage or are they hosted-only?

Mike (Billing PM): promo credits are scoped to hosted only today. Dedicated contracts usually have reserved allowances; we can apply one-off promotional balances via ops when approved.

Jon (Solutions Eng): can we document per-route priority exemption? customers want low-priority batch routes not to block critical API keys during quota exhaustion.

Riley (SRE): yes — routes can be marked priority: exempt, standard, or throttled. exempt routes bypass soft-degrade but still respect hard-credit caps. we'll add config examples to the runbook.

Nina (Customer Success): what's the visible signal for customers when soft degrade kicks in? some are worried they won't notice until failures spike.

Mike (Billing PM): Console shows a "soft cap active" banner plus email/webhook alerts. we also flag affected routes and sample requests in the usage timeline so teams can triage quickly.

Ava (Head of Product): important: what's the behavior if credits are added but haven't propagated yet and requests are made?

Riley (SRE): enforcement timeline: credit/top-up writes propagate in <90s typical. auth and rate-limit checks run before quota snapshot, so you can see transient 429/blocked responses if traffic occurs during propagation. best practice: schedule top-ups a minute before a launch.

Jon (Solutions Eng): for Private installs, can admins set a gracebuffer for local accounts? customers want a small buffer so long-running jobs don't die instantly.

Mike (Billing PM): Private supports a "gracebuffer" flag in the quota YAML that grants N extra token units for critical routes. it must be enabled by the admin and is audited. we'll publish the snippet.

Nina (Customer Success): refund policy: if a spike was due to our platform misrouting, how quickly can finance issue corrective credits?

Mike (Billing PM): standard timeline is investigation within 5 business days, provisional credits within 10 business days for confirmed platform faults, final reconciliation on the next invoice. escalate to billing@ for urgent cases.

Ava (Head of Product): clarification on billing units: how are embeddings billed relative to generation tokens in mixed calls?

Mike (Billing PM): embeddings consumed in a call are converted to embedding units at call completion and shown as a separate line item. mixed calls show both token and embedding lines. credits are debited from the same balance unless the account has split buckets configured.

Riley (SRE): question from infra: do retries after a 429 count toward rate-limit windows and quotas?

Mike (Billing PM): 429s don't consume credits. automated retry systems should use exponential backoff; retries that succeed will consume tokens as normal. note that retries can push you over burst thresholds so plan conservatively.

Jon (Solutions Eng): request: can we add a small example for self-serve burst increases and the payment requirement? customers keep asking how to do it quickly.

Mike (Billing PM): self-serve: Console -> Usage -> Temporary burst -> amount + duration -> requires payment method. For Dedicated we coordinate with CS. I'll draft a short step-by-step for the FAQ.

Ava (Head of Product): action list: Mike to draft the FAQ items (refund process, promo scope, burst flow), Riley to append propagation/429 note in rate-limit doc, Jon to collect customer examples for priority routes. we'll merge and publish.

Nina (Customer Success): I'll notify customers who asked and collect any edge cases. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
